headline: The web's newest weapon against AI scrapers is a font called ShieldFont
summary: ShieldFont subtly scrambles web page content for AI training models by replacing words in the underlying HTML, while keeping the displayed text perfectly readable for human users.
details: Designers Isaque Seneda and Gabriel Abrucio have introduced "ShieldFont," a new font designed to combat unauthorized AI data scraping. Its primary goal is to provide web publishers with a practical opt-out from having their content used for AI training.

ShieldFont leverages ligatures, a common font feature, to replace specific words in the underlying HTML with different ones. Crucially, this substitution only occurs when the font renders the page, meaning human readers see the original, correct text.

The font's strategy involves replacing words with others of a similar part of speech but a completely different informational context. For example, "horse" might be swapped with "potato," creating semantically incorrect but grammatically plausible sentences for scrapers.

After three months of refinement, the creators developed a dictionary of nearly 12,000 common words for ligature-based replacement. Publishers can choose from three different mapping options for each word, increasing the variability and making detection harder.
On average, ShieldFont replaces 24.5% of all words on a page, including 45.8% of "content words." This process mars the meaning of 31% to 56% of individual passages, depending on the text corpus.

In tests against six public scraper pipelines, ShieldFont caused over 90% of otherwise accepted pages to be rejected by quality filters. Even the small subset of pages that were still accepted contained nearly 20% "training-time garbage."

While effective against scrapers, using ShieldFont can have side effects for human-facing tools. Search engines, screen readers, copy/paste functions, and translation software may struggle with the altered underlying HTML.

The font isn't foolproof; AI scrapers employing optical character recognition (OCR) on rendered pages could bypass it. However, this method is significantly more expensive, estimated at five to 13 times the cost of standard HTML scraping.

ShieldFont primarily targets large-scale, indiscriminate HTML scraping, aiming to make it economically unfeasible for AI companies to gather vast amounts of clean training data. It adds a substantial cost and complexity barrier to current scraping practices.

headline_marked: [[Apple wins temporary Supreme Court pause]] in Epic Games proceedings
headline: Apple wins temporary Supreme Court pause in Epic Games proceedings
summary: The Supreme Court granted Apple a 24-hour extension to propose new commission rates for off-App Store purchases, a key development in its ongoing legal battle with Epic Games.
details: The Supreme Court has granted Apple a temporary 24-hour pause in its legal proceedings with Epic Games. This extension allows Apple more time to propose the commission rates it intends to charge on purchases made outside the App Store.

This development is part of the long-running antitrust dispute between Apple and Epic Games, which began when Epic challenged Apple's App Store policies by implementing its own payment system in Fortnite. The case has seen multiple appeals and rulings regarding Apple's control over its platform.
